{
  "B_expression": "-1/(2*(1+sqrt(1+r))**2)",
  "C_expression": "-(sqrt(1+r)+sqrt((1+u)*(1+u)+r)+u+2)/((sqrt(1+r)+sqrt((1+u)*(1+u)+r))*(sqrt((1+u)*(1+u)+r)+(1+u))*(sqrt(1+r)+1))",
  "derivation": "Retain B and use C to cancel the whole residual, not only the u=0 pure remainder. Let z=1+u, s=sqrt(1+r), S=sqrt(z^2+r). Since B gives r/2+r^2*B=s-1=r/(s+1), the submitted C is the regular rationalized form of [1/(S+z)-1/(s+1)]/u, i.e. C=-(s+S+z+1)/((s+S)*(S+z)*(s+1)). Therefore, where chi_r*chi_u=1, r^2*B+u*r*C = r/(s+1)+r*(1/(S+z)-1/(s+1))=r/(S+z)=S-z, so g=r/2+r^2*B+u*r*C=S-z. Then (z+g)^2-(z^2+r)=S^2-S^2=0. The formula has no division by u or r; at u=0 it reduces to the source-only step and at r=0 it gives g=0. On |r|<=1/2 and |u|<=1/4, z>=3/4 and S^2=z^2+r>=1/16, so all square roots and denominators are positive and the expression is smooth on a small open neighborhood without max or clipping. Exact cancellation is only inside the inner support where the host cutoff equals one; in the transition or outside support the same chi factor scales the whole added term, and chi=0 gives the bare r/2 update.",
  "inspect": [],
  "note": "Successor should expect the 2*u*g cross term to disappear numerically for rows with |r|<=1/4 and |u|<=1/8 (up to floating-point error), while transition rows and chi=0 rows retain their host-defined scaled/bare increments. Keep B unchanged. This is a smooth local coefficient-field correction for the two-slot quotient, not a global NS theorem; no all-order smoothness certificate is claimed from finite samples, and the archived R4 finite-root result keeps its separate scope."
